issues.claim: a part of older proxies and browsers does not cache URLs with a query string (RU: "а часть старых прокси и браузеров не кэширует URL со строкой запроса")
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt does not support this. Its caching note says the opposite: "The URI versioning and query string versioning schemas are cache-friendly because the same URI or query string combination refers to the same data each time." I cannot confirm that the current Azure page still carries the old warning about query strings. The same bullet also says the query string "caches naturally", so the answer is partly self-contradictory and may teach a stale claim as sourced.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the clause about older proxies and browsers, or reword it as general advice not attributed to the source, e.g. "query parameters can be ignored or normalised by some caches and CDNs, so check how yours treats them". Keep the cost of mixing the version with filter parameters. Make the same change in RU and EN.

issues.claim: UrlSegmentApiVersionReader, QueryStringApiVersionReader, HeaderApiVersionReader, MediaTypeApiVersionReader, ApiVersionReader.Combine, ReportApiVersions, api-supported-versions, api-deprecated-versions
issues.problem: These names exist in Asp.Versioning and are correct. The cited README excerpt does not list any of them, so the link supports them only generally. The note about the example header name `api-version` (the library's usual default is `api-version` for the query string and `x-api-version` for headers in samples) is also not stated in the answer.
issues.suggestedFix: Optionally add a link to the Asp.Versioning wiki page on version readers and the `api-supported-versions` header. Otherwise keep the text and state that the header name in the example is illustrative.

issues.problem: The facts are correct. Neither cited page covers JSON transcoding, so half of the answer has no source link. The grpcweb excerpt also does not show the "trailers" detail; the page says only that browsers do not give gRPC the needed control over HTTP/2. The trailers point is accurate, because fetch and XHR do not expose HTTP trailers.
issues.suggestedFix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/grpc/json-transcoding as a third link with a linkTitle in both locales.

issues.claim: Browser APIs (`fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`) do not give the control over HTTP/2 that gRPC needs, trailers in particular. You need gRPC-Web (`UseGrpcWeb`) or gRPC JSON transcoding.
issues.problem: The correct option is much longer than the distractors, which is a test-wiseness cue. The hint ("does the browser give page code access to everything gRPC sends in an HTTP/2 response?") nearly spells out the correct option.
issues.suggestedFix: Shorten option c and lengthen the distractors a little. Soften the hint, e.g. "What does gRPC need from the HTTP/2 layer that page code in a browser cannot control?"
